:::{#thm-kernel-same-mode}
#### A density and its kernel have the same modes

If $g$ is a [kernel of the density](#def-kernel) $f$ of a [random variable](#def-random-variable) $X$,
then $f$ and $g$ have the same [modes](#def-mode):

$$\modef{f} = \modef{g}.$$

Here the modes of $g$ are its [modes](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra.html#def-mode) as a [function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/functions.html#def-function) on $\rangef{X}$, since $g$ need not be a [density](#def-pdf).

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

Write $f(x) = c\, g(x)$ with $c > 0$ (@def-kernel).
By [the theorem that a positive multiple has the same argmax](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra.html#thm-argmax-positive-multiple),
$\argmax_{x \in \rangef{X}} f(x) = \argmax_{x \in \rangef{X}} g(x)$.
The left side is $\modef{f}$ by @def-mode,
and the right side is $\modef{g}$ by the definition of a [mode](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra.html#def-mode) of a [function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/functions.html#def-function).

:::
